ELEBAKE(8) System Manager’s Manual ELEBAKE(8)

NAME

elebake - compiler for a verified-boot trust chain: build, sign, attest, deploy, and the tamper-detection loader’s decisions

SYNOPSIS

elebake command [args ...]

elebake help [command | group | topic]

DESCRIPTION

elebake maintains the trust chain of a locally built FreeBSD boot loader: checked-out source, measured expectations, Authenticode signature, OpenPGP-attested manifest, deployment to removable boot media, and tamper witnesses read back at boot. Detection, not enforcement: the design assumes the boot medium can be tampered with and concentrates on noticing.

Every elebake command is a generator: it emits shell text describing an action. Whether that text is displayed, piped, or executed is decided by an interpreter the operator controls per function (see ENVIRONMENT). The shipped default displays (cat): inspect first, then pin an executing interpreter. Batch commands emit an unconditional sequence of further elebake commands; checking is itself a command in the sequence, and the batch machinery stops at the first failure.

The command reference below is generated from the tool’s own help corpus and is therefore always current; elebake help renders the same corpus in the terminal.

THE FREEBSD SOURCES

elebake is nothing without the loader it compiles for. The measurement, claim, gate and policy engine that reads the compiled decisions at boot is a FreeBSD patch series – platform trust gates – and the catalogs elebake offers (stage measure, stage action, stage when, stage phase show) are parsed from the headers of that series. Against a stock FreeBSD tree the catalogs are empty and no foundation can be built.

Get the tree that carries the series:

git clone -b platform-trust-gates-15.1 \


    https://github.com/johannes-bruegmann/freebsd-src.git ~/git/freebsd-src
elebake setenv ELEBAKE_FREEBSD_SRC ~/git/freebsd-src
elebake freebsd prerequisites

The branch is based on releng/15.1 (15.1-RELEASE); the loader-side engine lives under stand/efi/loader/local/ and its README points back at this project. Parts of the series are on their way upstream. stage checkout adds a git worktree of that repository per stage, so the source stays one repository and every stage builds from a named ref.

COMMANDS

Every command, grouped as elebake help groups it. elebake help <command> shows parameters, environment and examples.

Without a database

The only commands that run without an existing database. Start here.

bootstrap <path> <profile>
Create a new database at <path> with the named profile
help [<command|group|topic>]
Show the grouped overview, or detail for a command, group or topic
help manual
Emit the complete manual as Pandoc Markdown: prose building blocks from template/manual/, the COMMANDS reference from the help corpus, ENVIRONMENT from the variable templates – one truth per content kind (make man renders elebake.8 from it)
Inspect-by-default
Pipeline commands PRINT their shell: review, then append `| sh' to run (`| sudo sh' where the ESP or root-only keys are involved). Bookkeeping (add/bind/setenv/filter) is pinned to sh and acts directly. Experienced users may flip the safety default so EVERY terminal acts: elebake setenv ELEBAKE_TERMINAL_INTERPRETER sh (inspect any single command via setintp <family> cat, or per run under an explicit interpreter).

Configuration

Read and change elebake environment variables and interpreter pins.

environment init <profile>
Sync the profile’s variables template -> .env/default (idempotent; run after tool updates)
environment cache [on|off|status]
Manage the cached-environment optimisation
setenv <VAR> <VALUE>
Set a elebake environment variable (writes to .env/local/)
getenv <VAR>
Print the effective value of a variable with its source
unsetenv <VAR>
Remove a variable from .env/local/
printenv [<VAR>]
Show all effective environment variables, or just one
help env [<name> [location]]
Show env-var documentation (value + docs); with no argument, list all
setintp <function> <interpreter>
Pin a function’s interpreter (sugar for setenv ELEBAKE_INTERPRETER_*)
getintp <function>
Show a function’s pinned interpreter (sugar for getenv)
help intp <fn> [location]
Show docs for an interpreter variable (class default or per-function)

Database lifecycle

Back up, restore and batch-drive the database itself.

attest <file> <key>
Sign a file with a registered openpgp key: armored detached signature -> <file>.asc
attest verify <file> <key>
Check a detached signature at generation time: signed by the PINNED key, key neither expired nor revoked – a finding fails the command
destroy <name>
Remove this database and everything it owns, IRRECOVERABLY: the records, the worktrees and their registration in the source repo, the bundle handover area, the active-DB symlink
dump [<strategy>]
Export the database as an executable shell script; the bare form is the COMPLETE description (strategy `complete')
batch <file>
Execute a file of elebake commands line by line
restore <dump> [<base>]
Replay a dump into the current database – only a dump signed by the PINNED attest key, at or above the lineage’s serial; <base> binds where its base elements come from (default: this database)
collect [<stage>]
Fan out to every class: the complete list of files an archive must carry
filter <collection> <filtered>
Apply the default strategy to a collection (delegates: default -> redacted)
filter redacted <collection> <filtered>
Drop what is a machine secret in spirit: marker values, site.mk baselines, backups – and always the operational directories. What a bug report needs, without the reporter’s fingerprints
filter full <collection> <filtered>
Keep everything except the operational directories. For one’s own disaster recovery, never for sending
filter minimized <collection> <filtered>
Keep binary management only: per stage the loader (built and signed), loader.conf, kernel and modules, the manifest pair, media and backups; keys and receipts. What a rescue system needs to roll back or repair, nothing to build with
bundle <collection> <archive>
Pack the collected files: emits the packing command built from ELEBAKE_ARCHIVER, with the file list in a heredoc
seal <dump> <bundle>
Append the bundle’s sha256 to the dump as its seal line (`# Bundle: sha256=... bytes=...'); attest the dump AFTER sealing so one signature covers both
seal verify <dump> <bundle>
Check at generation time that the dump’s seal line names THIS bundle (sha256 and size) – a mismatch fails the command before anything is extracted
incoming clear <directory>
Empty one scratch directory under $ELEBAKE_ROOT/incoming/ – import’s own unpacking area, cleared before each extract so a re-import never trips over the last one
extract <archive> <destination>
Unpack an archive into a scratch directory: emits the unpacking command built from ELEBAKE_EXTRACTOR
export <dump> <bundle> <strategy> [<stage>]
Write the two artifacts that travel apart, bound and signed: the DUMP to a path of your choosing (commit it), the BUNDLE to its store. redacted/full describe the database COMPLETELY and govern the payload only; minimized describes and carries binary management only (the rescue pair)
import <dump> <bundle>
Replay an exported pair into the current database, checked end to end BEFORE anything lands: the seal (this bundle is the one the dump names), the bundle’s MANIFEST (pinned signer, every hash), the dump (pinned signer, serial); then restore and file the receipt
manifest <collection> <manifest>
Hash every entry of a collection into a manifest, same format as the boot manifest: LC_ALL=C-sorted `path sha256=hash' (symlinks as `path symlink=target')
manifest attest <collection> <key>
Write the manifest for a collection and sign it, side by side with the collection: manifest + attest
manifest verify <manifest> <base> <key>
Verify a manifest at generation time: signed by the PINNED key, signature good, tree matches – any finding fails the command
provenance serial
Advance the export serial by one (export does this before writing the dump); the number lands in the dump header
provenance add <dump> <bundle>
File the receipt of an admitted import: dump and bundle hashes, pinned signer, serial, when and where – same admissibility as restore – and raise the export serial to the imported one
provenance import <id> <absfile>
Copy ONE file of a receipt record from another database – dump/restore base element; the record directory is created on first file
provenance dump
Emit the provenance portion of a database dump: one `provenance import' line per receipt file (cat-pinned: dump TEXT, replayed by restore)
provenance collect
List the receipt record files that belong into an archive
provenance list
Show the export serial and every receipt: serial, when, signer, dump and bundle hashes, into which database

Keys

Key registries. Records hold REFERENCES (paths, URIs, key ids) – never private material; custody stays with the token, keyring, or root file.

openpgp add <name> <keyid> [<gnupghome>]
Register a GnuPG attest key; gnupghome for a keyring living elsewhere
openpgp dump
Emit the openpgp portion of a database dump: one `openpgp add' replay line per registered key
openpgp import <name> <absfile>
Copy ONE extra file into the key record — dump/restore base element (the schema files keyid/gnupghome travel as the `openpgp add' replay)
openpgp collect [<key>]
List the files of the openpgp key records that belong into an archive – public material only; private key material stays a path promise into the world
pem add <name> <keyfile> <certfile>
Register a file-based signing key by its paths (for sites without a token)
pem dump
Emit the pem portion of a database dump: one `pem add' replay line per registered key
pem import <name> <absfile>
Copy ONE extra file into the key record — dump/restore base element (the schema files key/cert travel as the `pem add' replay)
pem collect [<key>]
List the files of the pem key records that belong into an archive – public material only; private key material stays a path promise into the world
pkcs11 add <name> <uri> <certfile>
Register a PKCS#11 token key: its URI and certificate path
pkcs11 dump
Emit the pkcs11 portion of a database dump: one `pkcs11 add' replay line per registered key
pkcs11 import <name> <absfile>
Copy ONE extra file into the key record — dump/restore base element (the schema files uri/cert travel as the `pkcs11 add' replay)
pkcs11 collect [<key>]
List the files of the pkcs11 key records that belong into an archive – public material only; private key material stays a path promise into the world

Stage pipeline

A stage is one named workspace for one boot tree: bind keys, check out a worktree, embed trust, build isolated, curate, sign, attest.

stage list
List all stages with their derived state (one line each)
stage add <stage>
Create a named stage (workspace for one boot tree); IDEMPOTENT – an existing stage is left untouched
stage sign key <stage> <backend> <key>
Bind the loader-signing key slot (backend: pem | pkcs11)
stage attest key <stage> <backend> <key>
Bind the attest key slot (openpgp) – required BEFORE build: its anchor is embedded
stage unkey <stage>
Clear both key slots
stage status <stage>
Show the stage’s derived state (nothing cached – read from the artifacts)
stage sign <stage>
Authenticode-sign boot/loader.efi with the bound sign-key (pem: uefisign, pkcs11: osslsigncode)
stage attest <stage>
Detach-sign the stage manifest with the bound attest key
stage checkout <stage> <ref>
Add a git worktree of ELEBAKE_FREEBSD_SRC at <ref> and point the stage at it
stage clean <stage>
clean dir the worktree build and reset the stage’s build outputs
stage make <stage>
BUILD the stage: prereqs, clean, build stand, install, include, sign – publishing is stage push
stage build <stage>
prerequisites + clean + build stand: the isolated stand/ build
stage install <stage>
Unprivileged stand/ DESTDIR install into destdir/, per component (from the stage’s obj tree)
stage prerequisites exist add <stage> <path|->
Add one absolute bootfs path to the stage’s EXIST prerequisites (the loader claims its presence); `-' reads paths from stdin, one per line
stage prerequisites verify add <stage> <path|->
Add one absolute bootfs path to the stage’s VERIFY prerequisites (verified read against the manifest — presence AND integrity); `-' reads from stdin
stage prerequisites exist drop <stage> <path>
Remove one path from the stage’s EXIST prerequisites
stage prerequisites verify drop <stage> <path>
Remove one path from the stage’s VERIFY prerequisites
stage prerequisites exist show <stage>
Show the stage’s EXIST prerequisites list
stage prerequisites verify show <stage>
Show the stage’s VERIFY prerequisites list
stage build kernel <stage>
Build the kernel from the stage’s checkout (KERNCONF from ELEBAKE_KERNCONF, no implicit default; isolated per-stage obj) — the source delivers EVERYTHING, the filter selects
stage install kernel <stage>
Unprivileged installkernel into the stage’s destdir — destdir/boot/kernel becomes selectable by the filter
stage filter show <stage> [<srcdir>]
ONE view, the whole truth: the curated list, what sits uncurated in the source, what lies orphaned in boot/
stage filter add <stage> <rel|->
Curate one destdir/boot-relative path into the boot/ list (idempotent append); `-' reads a FROZEN snapshot from stdin, one path per line
stage filter drop <stage> <rel>
Remove one entry from the boot/ curation list
stage include <stage> [<srcdir>]
Work the curated filter off from a chosen SOURCE directory (default: the stage’s own destdir/boot; e.g. /boot takes the same selection from the host’s binaries)
stage adopt <stage> <medium> <gpt-label> <pool/dataset>
One-time adoption: copy the medium’s boot tree into the stage – boot/ becomes the single source of truth
stage loader <stage> <loader.efi>
Ingest an ALREADY-BUILT external loader as boot/loader.efi – sign it without building
stage manifest <stage>
Generate the REAL veriexec manifest over boot/ (path sha256=hash; includes loader.efi as disaster reserve)
stage verify <stage>
Manifest consistency BOTH ways, checked at generation time: listed entries must match, unlisted files are findings
stage trust anchor <stage>
Export the attest key + self-test signature into the worktree’s libsecureboot
stage trust mk <stage>
Write site.trust.mk (elevated veriexec config) into the worktree
stage source <stage>
trust anchor + trust mk in one step
stage push <stage> <medium>
Publish the stage: manifest, attest, verify, tree onto the medium, loader onto the ESP
stage edit <stage> <relpath>
Edit a file of the stage’s boot tree (the single source of truth); publish with stage push
stage site mk report <stage>
Show the stage’s written site.mk (comment lines; the batch shows it after measuring)
stage dump [<stage> [<strategy>]]
Emit the dump of all stages (or one) as replayable elebake commands — per stage: check stage, then the cat-pinned building blocks dump record/dump marker/dump backup/dump boot/dump rebuild; `minimized' narrows to binary management (no marker, no rebuild, boot/ subset)
stage import <stage> <reldir> [<absfile>]
Import ONE base element from another database: two args declare a record-tree DIRECTORY, three copy a file/symlink into it — an unconditional check-then-act sequence; the logic lives in the dump that emits these lines
stage collect [<stage>]
List the files of every stage record that belong into an archive: metadata, filter, key bindings, marker/, backup/, boot/, phases/, prereqs/, conf/ – plus the name symlink LAST, because a link target must exist before the link

Provisioning

The machine-bound trust expectations: the NVRAM boot marker and the compiled-in baselines (local/site.mk). What turns a generic loader into THIS machine’s tamper detector.

stage marker <stage> <BootXXXX|new> [<filepath>]
Write the boot-entry marker: BootXXXX targets that load option, `new' rotates the value; filepath (re)records the value file
stage site mk <stage>
Measure THIS machine at generation time; write + report the local/site.mk baselines

Medium

The physical boot medium: bind it, back up its loader, swap, roll back.

stage device <stage> <medium> </dev/node> [<mountpoint>]
Register a NAMED deploy medium; its backups sort under backup/<medium>
stage backup <stage> <medium> [<label> [<description>]]
Save the loader currently ON that medium as a backup RECORD backup/<medium>/<label>/ – loader.efi, description, sha256, created, source, by. Label defaults to the UTC stamp, description to medium/stage/user; a label is unique per medium and immutable
stage backup list <stage> <medium>
Show the backup records of that medium, oldest first: label, created, sha256, description – the view for a rollback decision
stage deploy <stage> <medium>
The loader swap onto the NAMED medium: mount, backup, copy, verify, umount
stage rollback <stage> <medium> [<label>]
Put a backup back onto the medium – but FIRST save what is on the medium now as record suspect-<stamp> (quietly: the loader about to be overwritten may be the evidence), then write the named (or newest) backup and verify its hash on the medium
stage boot tree <stage> <medium> <gpt-label> <pool/dataset>
Register where the medium’s boot tree lives (used by stage push/tree sync)
stage tree sync <stage> <medium>
Write the stage’s boot/ tree onto the medium’s dataset – snapshot first, verify in place, export

Trust foundation (catalogs and, soon, claims/gates/policies)

Toolchain readiness checks; each backend answers for itself.

macro add <MACRO> <type> <label> [<else>] [<defined>]
Store a build-provided baseline slot: site.mk may deliver -DLOADER_TRUST_<MACRO>, absent selects the #else alternative (identical re-add is a no-op)
macro drop <MACRO>
Remove a macro record (free; dangling expectation references are verify’s business)
macro show [<MACRO>]
Show all macro records (or one) as the #ifdef block that WOULD be emitted
expectation add <exp> <type> <label> <value>
Store a named, reusable measured-value expectation (DB-wide arsenal; identical re-add is a no-op, a differing one is refused)
expectation drop <exp>
Remove an expectation (free; dangling references are verify’s business)
expectation show [<exp>]
Show all expectations (or one) as the C that WOULD be emitted
claim add <claim> <measurement> <diagnose|-> <publish|-> <exp>
Store a named, reusable claim referencing an expectation (may dangle until bound; identical re-add is a no-op)
claim drop <claim>
Remove a claim (free; dangling gate references are verify’s business)
claim show [<claim>]
Show all claims (or one) as the C that WOULD be emitted
trigger add <trigger> <when> <action>
Store a named, reusable FIRE(<when>, &<action>) pair (identical re-add is a no-op)
trigger drop <trigger>
Remove a trigger (free; dangling policy references are verify’s business)
trigger show [<trigger>]
Show all triggers (or one) as the C that WOULD be emitted
gate add <gate> [<secret-slot>]
Create a gate record (secret-slot NAMES the -D macro, never a value; identical re-add is a no-op)
gate drop <gate>
Remove a gate record (free; dangling policy references are verify’s business)
gate claim add <gate> <claim> [<position>]
Append a claim reference to a gate (order = evaluation order; may dangle; 3-arg form inserts at a 1-based position)
gate claim drop <gate> <claim>
Unlink a claim reference from a gate (the claim itself survives)
gate show [<gate>]
Show all gates (or one) as the C that WOULD be emitted
policy add <policy> <gate>
Create a named policy for a gate (triggers appended separately; may dangle; identical re-add is a no-op)
policy trigger add <policy> <trigger> [<position>]
Append a trigger (FIRE) reference to a policy; 3-arg form inserts at a 1-based position
policy trigger drop <policy> <trigger>
Remove a trigger reference from a policy (the trigger itself survives)
policy drop <policy>
Remove a policy (free; dangling phase references are verify’s business)
policy show [<policy>]
Show all policies (or one) as the C that WOULD be emitted
foundation collect
List the arsenal record files (macros, expectations, claims, triggers, gates, policies) that belong into an archive
stage measure <stage>
List the measurement (and diagnose) functions the stage’s checkout offers — the catalog claims may reference; new offers are C patches, not elebake input
stage action <stage>
List the actions the stage’s checkout offers (policy FIRE targets)
stage when <stage>
List the firing predicates the stage’s checkout offers
stage phase show <stage> [<phase>]
List the phases the stage’s checkout offers, each with its BOUND policies (records); one phase in detail with the 2-arg form
stage phase policy add <stage> <phase> <policy> [<position>]
Bind a policy to a stage’s phase — validates the policy’s transitive chain (gate, claims, expectations, triggers, whens, actions) against the checkout’s catalog, then appends; 4-arg form inserts at a 1-based position
stage phase policy drop <stage> <phase> <policy>
Unbind a policy from a stage’s phase (the policy itself survives)
stage foundation check <stage>
Sharp re-verification of every bound phase right before emission: phases still in the enum, every policy chain complete and in the checkout’s catalog (the world may have drifted)
stage foundation make <stage>
Generate foundation.c from the bound policies into the worktree (generated-only file; check first — this terminal renders what the records say)
stage foundation report <stage>
Summarize the foundation of a stage: bound phases, their policies, the referenced gates/claims and the emission target
stage foundation <stage>
The foundation batch: check stage -> foundation check -> foundation make -> foundation report

ENVIRONMENT

All configuration lives in ELEBAKE_* variables, layered as .env/local (override, written by setenv), .env/default (the installed profile) and the shipped templates. Interpreter pins ELEBAKE_INTERPRETER_<function> decide per function whether emitted shell is displayed or executed: arity-specific before arity-agnostic before the class default (ELEBAKE_TERMINAL_INTERPRETER, default cat). Every variable answers elebake help env <VAR>.

ELEBAKE_ARCHIVE_ATTEST_KEY
The openpgp record that signs what this database exports – and the signer a receiver expects
ELEBAKE_FREEBSD_PREREQUISITES
Curated tool list freebsd prerequisites probes at generation time
ELEBAKE_FREEBSD_SRC
Path to the FreeBSD source repository the stages build from
ELEBAKE_INCLUDES
Modules preloaded at startup (engine.sh is always loaded first)
ELEBAKE_INTERPRETER_attest
Interpreter for attest – produces <file>.asc
ELEBAKE_INTERPRETER_attest_verify
Interpreter for attest verify – the pinned signature check
ELEBAKE_INTERPRETER_filter_minimized
Interpreter for filter minimized – writes the rescue collection
ELEBAKE_INTERPRETER_help_manual
Interpreter for help manual – Pandoc Markdown on stdout
ELEBAKE_INTERPRETER_incoming_clear
Interpreter for incoming clear – empties import’s scratch directory
ELEBAKE_INTERPRETER_manifest
Interpreter for manifest – writes the MANIFEST file
ELEBAKE_INTERPRETER_manifest_verify
Interpreter for manifest verify – signature and hashes
ELEBAKE_INTERPRETER_provenance_add
Interpreter for provenance add – files the receipt of an import
ELEBAKE_INTERPRETER_provenance_collect
Interpreter for provenance collect – receipt files for an archive
ELEBAKE_INTERPRETER_provenance_dump
Interpreter for provenance dump – dump TEXT
ELEBAKE_INTERPRETER_provenance_import
Interpreter for provenance import – restore base element
ELEBAKE_INTERPRETER_provenance_list
Interpreter for provenance list – the lineage, readable
ELEBAKE_INTERPRETER_provenance_serial
Interpreter for provenance serial – advances export/serial
ELEBAKE_INTERPRETER_seal
Interpreter for seal – appends the bundle hash to the dump
ELEBAKE_INTERPRETER_seal_verify
Interpreter for seal verify – dump names THIS bundle?
ELEBAKE_INTERPRETER_stage_backup4
Interpreter for stage backup (the arity-4 act terminal ONLY)
ELEBAKE_INTERPRETER_stage_backup_list
Interpreter for stage backup list – the rollback decision view
ELEBAKE_INTERPRETER_stage_rollback_apply
Interpreter for stage rollback apply – the write onto the medium

FILES

~/.elebake/db
the active database (symlink)
~/.elebake/<name>/.env/{local,default}/
the layered variable store: overrides (setenv) over the installed profile over the shipped templates
~/.elebake/<name>/.log/YYYY-MM-DD/
per-invocation traces – the debugging ground truth (elebake last)
~/.elebake/<name>/stage/<stage>/
a stage record: boot/ (the built tree), backup/<medium>/<label>/ (backup records), media/, marker/
~/.elebake/<name>/provenance/
receipts of every admitted import (the lineage)
~/.elebake/worktree/
git worktrees of the FreeBSD source; build trees live outside the database
~/.elebake/bundle/, ~/.elebake/incoming/
where an exported bundle is handed to the user, and import’s scratch area

EXAMPLES

Create a database, connect the sources, register keys, build and publish a stage:

./elebake.sh bootstrap current minimal | sh
./elebake.sh setenv ELEBAKE_FREEBSD_SRC ~/git/freebsd-src
./elebake.sh pkcs11 add db 'pkcs11:token=...;object=db' /root/sb/db.crt
./elebake.sh openpgp add manifest 4E1F0A2B7C9D8E6F5A4B3C2D1E0F9A8B7C6D5E4F /root/sb/.gnupg
./elebake.sh stage add smoke1
./elebake.sh stage sign key smoke1 pkcs11 db
./elebake.sh stage attest key smoke1 openpgp manifest
./elebake.sh stage checkout smoke1 platform-trust-gates-15.1^0 | sh
./elebake.sh stage make smoke1
./elebake.sh stage push smoke1 b

Take the database elsewhere – one signed pair, pinned on arrival:

./elebake.sh setenv ELEBAKE_ARCHIVE_ATTEST_KEY manifest
./elebake.sh export ~/git/config/dump.sh ~/.elebake/bundle/a1b2c3d.tar.gz full
# on the receiving machine
./elebake.sh openpgp add manifest 4E1F0A2B7C9D8E6F5A4B3C2D1E0F9A8B7C6D5E4F
./elebake.sh setenv ELEBAKE_ARCHIVE_ATTEST_KEY manifest
./elebake.sh import ~/git/config/dump.sh ~/.elebake/bundle/a1b2c3d.tar.gz
./elebake.sh provenance list

The rescue pair, and a rollback that keeps the evidence:

./elebake.sh export ~/rescue/dump.sh ~/rescue/bundle.tar.gz minimized
./elebake.sh stage backup list smoke1 a
./elebake.sh stage rollback smoke1 a known-good-p2

Inspect instead of act (any command): run it while the terminal default is cat, read the emitted shell, then re-run under an executing pin.
